audience_note: Describes a colonial military attack and the looting of cultural property from the Edo royal palace, preceded by the deaths of British officials and African servants and porters. The objects remain the focus of debate about restitution; the Peabody Museum acknowledges the violence and trauma of the Expedition.
title: British Expedition to Benin City (1897)
summary: In January 1897 seven British officials and most of their African servants and porters were killed in an ambush on the way to Benin City. Britain then sent a "punitive expedition" of 1200 troops, who occupied and looted the royal palace of the Edo Kingdom, taking an estimated 3000 to 5000 objects, many later auctioned by the Admiralty.

as_recorded.value: 1897 British Colonial Military Campaign on Benin

where.historical_name: Benin City, capital of the Edo Kingdom (Kingdom of Benin)

importance.justification: The looting dispersed thousands of Benin objects to European and North American museums and is central to present restitution debates, per National Museums Scotland.

sources.title: Peabody Museum Statement on Material from Benin City
sources.publisher: Harvard University, Peabody Museum of Archaeology and Ethnology

reviewer_note: Object count is the NMS estimate (3000-5000), not reconciled with other published figures. Neither opened page gives an exact day for the attack, so precision is year. Neutral wording; the British framing as a punitive response is reported as NMS reports it.
